nodes.description: OER performance in 1.0 M KOH at 25°C
nodes.source_text: the heterostructure demonstrates an ultralow overpotential, requiring merely 202 mV to reach a current density of 10 mA cm⁻², significantly outperforming NiFe-LDH (234 mV), Ni₃S₂ (288 mV), and NM (313 mV). The NiFe-LDH/Ni₃S₂ heterostructure exhibits a low Tafel slope of 45.1 mV dec⁻¹... The NiFe-LDH/Ni₃S₂ heterostructure displays the smallest charge-transfer resistance (R_ct)... The C_dl value of NiFe-LDH/Ni₃S₂ is calculated to be 1.96 mF cm⁻²... NiFe-LDH/Ni₃S₂ shows a negligible degradation in OER activity over an extended period exceeding 200 h at a high current density of 800 mA cm⁻²... After 2000 cycles, the catalyst exhibits only a modest increase in overpotential by 30 and 34 mV at 10 and 800 mA cm⁻²

Two-electrode stability test with Raney Ni cathode (30 wt% KOH, 80°C)
nodes.source_text: Coupled with a Raney Ni cathode, the NiFe-LDH/Ni₃S₂ anode exhibits minimal degradation of cell voltage after a 100-h test at 300 mA cm⁻²

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows Ni₃S₂ enhances surface roughness on NM for NiFe-LDH deposition; NiFe-LDH/Ni₃S₂ shows uniform NiFe-LDH distribution. Cross-sectional SEM reveals ≈200 nm Ni₃S₂ layer and ≈300 nm NiFe-LDH layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The in situ growth of Ni₃S₂ on the NM surface enhances the surface roughness (Figure 1c), thereby providing an enhanced adhesion strength for the deposition of NiFe-LDH. SEM image and elemental mapping confirm the uniform distribution of NiFe-LDH on the Ni₃S₂ layer (Figure 1d,e). Cross-sectional SEM analysis discloses a ≈200-nm Ni₃S₂ layer atop the NM, capped by a ≈300-nm NiFe-LDH layer.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images and elemental mapping show intimate interfacial coupling between Ni₃S₂ and NiFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images and elemental mapping elucidate the intimate interfacial coupling between Ni₃S₂ and NiFe-LDH (Figure 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals strongly coupled heterointerface between Ni₃S₂ and NiFe-LDH with distinct lattice fringes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image (Figure 1h, Figure S3) with distinct lattice fringes further reveals the strongly coupled heterointerface between Ni₃S₂ and NiFe-LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping from SEM confirms uniform Ni, Fe distribution in NiFe-LDH/Ni₃S₂; post-CP TEM/EDS shows even Ni, Fe distribution maintained.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM image and elemental mapping confirm the uniform distribution of NiFe-LDH on the Ni₃S₂ layer (Figure 1d,e)... TEM images after the CP test confirm an even distribution of Ni and Fe in the heterostructure (Figure 4f).

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS shows work function of 3.01 eV for Ni₃S₂ and 2.48 eV for NiFe-LDH, indicating ΔΦ of 0.53 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: UPS was utilized to obtain work functions (Φ) values of Ni₃S₂ and NiFe-LDH (Figure 2a). The calculated Φ values are 3.01 eV for Ni₃S₂ and 2.48 eV for NiFe-LDH, indicating a substantial ΔΦ of 0.53 eV...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni 2p and Fe 2p binding energies shift upward by 0.5 eV and 0.4 eV in NiFe-LDH/Ni₃S₂ compared to NiFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiFe-LDH/Ni₃S₂ shows upward shifts of 0.5 and 0.4 eV of the binding energy in the Ni 2p and Fe 2p region compared with those of NiFe-LDH, respectively (Figure 2b,c)...

nodes.characterization_summary: UV/Vis DRS shows NiFe-LDH/Ni₃S₂ heterostructure possesses narrower bandgap than Ni₃S₂ due to incorporation with NiFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: UV/Vis DRS shows that the heterostructure possesses a narrower bandgap than that of Ni₃S₂, an effect attributed to the incorporation between the Ni₃S₂ transition layer and NiFe-LDH (Figure 2d, Figure S4).

properties.description: Bandgap determination plot (Ahv² vs bandgap energy)

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows NO₃⁻ intercalation confirming NiFe-LDH identity, Fe-O signal reduction at high potential due to Fe leaching in NiFe-LDH but maintained in NiFe-LDH/Ni₃S₂, and Ni-O peaks shifting to γ-NiOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of interlayer anion intercalation, indicated by the NO₃⁻ signal, affirms the identity of NiFeLDH... Compared with NiFe-LDH/Ni₃S₂, the Fe-O signal in NiFe-LDH is significantly reduced at high potential due to overoxidation and Fe leaching.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS shows rapid Fe leaching from NiFe-LDH but slow Fe leaching from NiFe-LDH/Ni₃S₂ during CP tests at 800 mA cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP-MS monitored the amount of Fe dissolution... The results show that NiFe-LDH exhibits rapid Fe leaching, and by the introduction of BEF, a slow Fe leaching is displayed in NiFe-LDH/Ni₃S₂ (Figure 4c).

properties.description: Full cell configuration: NiFe-LDH/Ni3S2 anode || PPS separator || Raney Ni cathode

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman before/after CP shows NiFe-LDH/Ni₃S₂ retains Fe-O and NO₃⁻ signals while NiFe-LDH shows diminished signals indicating Fe loss.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectroscopy before and after CP tests reveals that while both NiFe-LDH/Ni₃S₂ and NiFe-LDH undergo NiOOH reconstruction, the former retains a discernible Fe-O peak and NO₃⁻ signal (Figure 4d).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows NiFe-LDH/Ni₃S₂ has smallest charge-transfer resistance (R_ct) indicating fastest charge transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The NiFe-LDH/Ni₃S₂ heterostructure displays the smallest charge-transfer resistance (R_ct) in the EIS Nyquist plots, indicative of the fastest charge transfer among all samples (Figure 3c).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at various scan rates gives C_dl = 1.96 mF cm⁻² for NiFe-LDH/Ni₃S₂, larger than NiFe-LDH, Ni₃S₂, and NM.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The C_dl value of NiFe-LDH/Ni₃S₂ is calculated to be 1.96 mF cm⁻², noticeably larger than those of NiFe-LDH, Ni₃S₂, and NM (Figure 3d, Figure S8).
